bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Credit risk in the Financial Services (L&T Finance) book — Credit risk — transactional (default) and portfolio (intrinsic/concentration) — is described as central to L&T Finance's strategy; the retail loan book was 98% of the total loan book as at March 31, 2026, with disbursements up 38% y-o-y, meaning asset-quality outcomes are increasingly tied to rapid retail scaling.
- Model / algorithmic decisioning risk — Growing reliance on AI-driven engines (Project Cyclops for underwriting, Project Nostradamus for early-warning signals) across credit origination and portfolio monitoring means inaccuracies in these models could mis-price or mis-detect credit risk; a dedicated Model Risk Management Committee was set up to govern this exposure.
- Liquidity / funding-market risk — Heightened volatility in funding markets, fuelled by shifting global trade dynamics and geopolitical conflict, raises the risk of insufficient liquid assets to meet obligations, particularly for the Financial Services business.
- Geopolitical risk / West Asia disruption — A disruption in West Asia that began in February 2026 creates uncertainty for the global economy; India's FY2026-27 GDP growth outlook (projected at 6.9%) carries explicit downside risk from the Gulf conflict, and West Asia is a strategically important market/order source for the Group.
- IT / cyber security risk — Increasing digitisation of business applications and algorithm-driven decisioning raises exposure to ransomware, malware and data leakage; the Board Risk Management Committee's terms of reference explicitly include evaluating cyber-security risk, and L&T Finance runs a dedicated Infosec function under an ISO 27001:2022-certified ISMS.
- Enterprise-wide strategic, operational and regulatory risk — The Company operates a structured enterprise risk management framework overseen by the Board Risk Management Committee, covering strategic, operational, financial, regulatory and sustainability-related risks across domestic and international operations, including market, geographical, political and reputational issues.
- Sector-wide unsecured-lending / asset-quality stress (system-level) — RBI has flagged that unsecured loans (personal loans, credit cards) accounted for 53.1% of all retail loan slippages system-wide, with private banks seeing 76% of fresh slippage from this segment, and elevated impairment among borrowers with unsecured loans from five-plus lenders amid rapid fintech credit expansion (36.1% y-o-y) — a system-level vigilance area relevant to L&T Finance's operating environment.
- Climate risk in Rural/Farmer Finance portfolios — L&T Finance analyses rainfall deviation and reservoir storage capacity to manage climate-linked risk primarily within its Rural Business and Farmer Finance portfolios, with climate considerations now embedded in decision-making and periodic portfolio assessments.

outlook.body: Project execution and commissioning milestones during FY2025-26 spanned Infrastructure, Energy and Hi-Tech Manufacturing: Phase 1 of the Navi Mumbai International Airport was inaugurated; Phase 1 of Patna Medical College & Hospital, Bihar was inaugurated (on full completion it is expected to become the world's second-largest hospital); the Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) of 3.55 MMTPA capacity was commissioned for HPCL at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh; all facilities under the Marjan Increment Package 2 project for Saudi Aramco were energised; the Daman Upside Development Project was completed for ONGC; the BGEPIL Tapti Decommissioning Project was completed as India's first full-scale offshore decommissioning initiative; Commercial Operation Declaration (COD) was achieved for Unit-1 of the 2x660 MW SJVN thermal power plant at Buxar, Bihar and for Unit-2 of the 2x660 MW Khurja super thermal power plant, Uttar Pradesh; commercial operations began on the entire 182-TKM mainline of the Delhi-Meerut RRTS; the 112.5 MW Goaltore solar power plant in West Bengal was inaugurated as one of the largest renewable power projects in eastern India; a 156 km transmission line connecting Rooppur and Gopalganj was successfully beamed, boosting Bangladesh's energy infrastructure; HZL's Debari Roaster #6 was commissioned, expanding smelting operations; 12 Stackers and Reclaimers were commissioned; and a 1,100 TPH aggregate crushing plant was commissioned at Fujairah, UAE. Significant milestones were also achieved at the Rajasthan Atomic Power Plant (RAPP) units 7 & 8, with the Natural Draught Cooling Towers (NDCTs) and related works being executed ahead of schedule. Separately, the Indian cement industry (an end-market for the Minerals & Metals Product business) is projected to add approximately 50-60 MTPA of new capacity in FY2026-27, with further additions planned in subsequent years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Record order inflow growth driven by strong investment momentum in West Asia, sustained policy-led capex impetus by the Government of India, and increasing participation of private-sector enterprises in the domestic market
- Group revenue growth primarily driven by execution progress across project and manufacturing businesses, with rising share of international revenue reflecting strong execution and order conversion in overseas markets
- Construction & Mining Machinery: government's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM Gati Shakti programmes expected to generate robust demand for construction equipment; coal expected to retain a central role in India's energy mix supporting mining-equipment demand; sustained government infrastructure spend expected to keep cement/steel demand healthy
- L&T Valves: medium- to long-term outlook remains structurally positive, supported by investments in energy security, infrastructure development and industrial capacity expansion; downstream oil & gas, petrochemicals, LNG infrastructure and water-project investments expected to continue; defence and nuclear segments present long-term opportunities via indigenisation
- L&T Construction Equipment: outlook stable, supported by continued investment in infrastructure, mining and urban development, with replacement demand and localisation trends providing additional demand stability
- Rubber Processing Machinery: global tyre demand expected to grow steadily on replacement demand and gradual EV penetration; India's tyre industry expected to sustain growth on infrastructure-led freight movement and export orientation, though near-term capex by developed-market tyre makers remains selective
- Energy-transition-linked investments such as large-scale carbon capture projects moderated in the latter half of FY2025-26, resulting in more selective project sanctioning by developers
- Tariff-related developments and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties led to delays and deliberate deferrals in order finalisation across some businesses
- The evolving situation in West Asia creates near-term uncertainty but the region continues to be closely monitored, with restoration of normalcy seen as a potential source of rebuilding and investment opportunities over time
- Record consolidated order book of Rs 7,40,327 crore as at March 31, 2026, up 27.8% y-o-y, providing strong multi-year revenue visibility for the Group
- Infrastructure Projects remained the largest contributor to the consolidated order book at 57% as at year-end
- Around 61% of the total order book as at March 2026 comprised orders from Government of India, state governments/local authorities and public sector enterprises; the private-sector share increased to 39% from 28% a year earlier
- About 19% of the domestic order book is funded by multilateral agencies
- Share of international orders in the consolidated order book increased from 46% to 52% on higher international order intake
- L&T Group achieved record order inflow of Rs 4,35,590 crore in FY2025-26, growth of 22.1% y-o-y and the highest in the Company's history, with international orders at 58% of total inflow

business_model.body: Larsen & Toubro operates through Infrastructure Projects (EPC of buildings & factories, transportation infrastructure, heavy civil infrastructure, power transmission & distribution, renewables, water & effluent treatment, and minerals & metals), Energy Projects (hydrocarbon onshore/offshore EPC covering oil & gas, refineries, petrochemicals and offshore wind, plus CarbonLite Solutions for power-generation BTG scope and carbon capture) and Hi-Tech Manufacturing (Heavy Engineering for process plants and nuclear energy; Precision Engineering and Systems for marine/land defence platforms, aerospace and space). Government and related entities are the primary customers (~65% of revenue), with the balance from domestic and international private-sector clients; roughly 67% of revenue is domestic and 33% international, with the GCC region (about a third of annual revenue) a particularly important market.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Record order inflow growth driven by strong investment momentum in West Asia, sustained policy-led capex impetus by the Government of India, and increasing participation of private-sector enterprises in the domestic market
- Group revenue growth primarily driven by execution progress across project and manufacturing businesses, with rising share of international revenue reflecting strong execution and order conversion in overseas markets
- Construction & Mining Machinery: government's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, National Infrastructure Pipeline and PM Gati Shakti programmes expected to generate robust demand for construction equipment; coal expected to retain a central role in India's energy mix supporting mining-equipment demand; sustained government infrastructure spend expected to keep cement/steel demand healthy
- L&T Valves: medium- to long-term outlook remains structurally positive, supported by investments in energy security, infrastructure development and industrial capacity expansion; downstream oil & gas, petrochemicals, LNG infrastructure and water-project investments expected to continue; defence and nuclear segments present long-term opportunities via indigenisation
- L&T Construction Equipment: outlook stable, supported by continued investment in infrastructure, mining and urban development, with replacement demand and localisation trends providing additional demand stability
- Rubber Processing Machinery: global tyre demand expected to grow steadily on replacement demand and gradual EV penetration; India's tyre industry expected to sustain growth on infrastructure-led freight movement and export orientation, though near-term capex by developed-market tyre makers remains selective
- Energy-transition-linked investments such as large-scale carbon capture projects moderated in the latter half of FY2025-26, resulting in more selective project sanctioning by developers
- Tariff-related developments and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties led to delays and deliberate deferrals in order finalisation across some businesses
- The evolving situation in West Asia creates near-term uncertainty but the region continues to be closely monitored, with restoration of normalcy seen as a potential source of rebuilding and investment opportunities over time
- Record consolidated order book of Rs 7,40,327 crore as at March 31, 2026, up 27.8% y-o-y, providing strong multi-year revenue visibility for the Group
- Infrastructure Projects remained the largest contributor to the consolidated order book at 57% as at year-end
- Around 61% of the total order book as at March 2026 comprised orders from Government of India, state governments/local authorities and public sector enterprises; the private-sector share increased to 39% from 28% a year earlier
- About 19% of the domestic order book is funded by multilateral agencies
- Share of international orders in the consolidated order book increased from 46% to 52% on higher international order intake
- L&T Group achieved record order inflow of Rs 4,35,590 crore in FY2025-26, growth of 22.1% y-o-y and the highest in the Company's history, with international orders at 58% of total inflow

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Projects & Manufacturing EBITDA margin down 80 bps YoY to 8.2% due to job mix, close-out costs (two projects), and legacy procurement at high commodity prices; cost pressures from energy, design changes, and delayed sourcing; margin recovery expected in H2 due to favorable new procurement and project milestones

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing debt reduction in Hyderabad Metro (target: Rs.7.5-8T from Rs.13T over 24 months via Rs.3T govt interest-free loan and Rs.2-2.5T TOD monetization); divesting non-core assets (Nabha, L&T IDPL); maintaining strong balance sheet (CRAR 22.6%, net debt-equity 0.89); reinvesting in strategic growth areas (green tech, digital)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Project execution and commissioning milestones during FY2025-26 spanned Infrastructure, Energy and Hi-Tech Manufacturing: Phase 1 of the Navi Mumbai International Airport was inaugurated; Phase 1 of Patna Medical College & Hospital, Bihar was inaugurated (on full completion it is expected to become the world's second-largest hospital); the Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) of 3.55 MMTPA capacity was commissioned for HPCL at Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh; all facilities under the Marjan Increment Package 2 project for Saudi Aramco were energised; the Daman Upside Development Project was completed for ONGC; the BGEPIL Tapti Decommissioning Project was completed as India's first full-scale offshore decommissioning initiative; Commercial Operation Declaration (COD) was achieved for Unit-1 of the 2x660 MW SJVN thermal power plant at Buxar, Bihar and for Unit-2 of the 2x660 MW Khurja super thermal power plant, Uttar Pradesh; commercial operations began on the entire 182-TKM mainline of the Delhi-Meerut RRTS; the 112.5 MW Goaltore solar power plant in West Bengal was inaugurated as one of the largest renewable power projects in eastern India; a 156 km transmission line connecting Rooppur and Gopalganj was successfully beamed, boosting Bangladesh's energy infrastructure; HZL's Debari Roaster #6 was commissioned, expanding smelting operations; 12 Stackers and Reclaimers were commissioned; and a 1,100 TPH aggregate crushing plant was commissioned at Fujairah, UAE. Significant milestones were also achieved at the Rajasthan Atomic Power Plant (RAPP) units 7 & 8, with the Natural Draught Cooling Towers (NDCTs) and related works being executed ahead of schedule. Separately, the Indian cement industry (an end-market for the Minerals & Metals Product business) is projected to add approximately 50-60 MTPA of new capacity in FY2026-27, with further additions planned in subsequent years.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on India/GCC growth tailwinds and order book visibility; cautiously optimistic on margin recovery in H2; transparent about headwinds (costs, supply chain); committed to capital efficiency and ROE improvement via divestments and restructuring; avoiding overpromising on guidance

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Client relationships in the GCC built over decades of trust, delivery and transparency, sustaining business continuity through the regional conflict with no material disruption to invoicing or collections
- Integrated end-to-end capabilities across the value chain — dedicated engineering design centres, project management systems, procurement practices and specialised technical services
- Decades-long expertise in engineering and manufacturing critical reactors and pressure vessels, including for the nuclear sector
- Market leadership in core EPC construction businesses
- Shop modernisation using robots/cobots in Heavy Engineering delivering productivity gains — e.g. a single operator can now simultaneously run three overlay welds

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Elevated inflation and input cost volatility; supply chain disruptions; global recession impacting IT spends; delayed state capex awards; currency depreciation; delays in divestments (Nabha, IDPL); margin slippage in fixed-price contracts; geopolitical instability in GCC

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Hyderabad Metro's EBITDA margin of 39% is driven by operational efficiency, not revenue growth alone; ridership surge (441K/day) is a leading indicator for future cash flow stability; L&T's 85% variable-price infrastructure contracts provide natural inflation hedge; private sector order prospects up 10% YoY signals structural shift in India's capex dynamics

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Maximising shareholder value by divesting identified non-core assets
- Driving operational excellence through digital initiatives to enhance cost competitiveness
- Strengthening working capital discipline and funds management
- Ensuring effective and profitable execution of the robust order book
- Reorganised the Hydrocarbon business into three distinct units — Onshore, Offshore and Offshore Wind — for focused execution
- Consolidated data center operations under the Larsen & Toubro Vyoma brand (previously L&T-Cloudfiniti), extending core engineering and manufacturing expertise into the digital economy …
